subject: MAP: regional resilience validation & close cadence
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan@streamline.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial ask: MAP + regional perf validation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo today — the throughput and routing features look promising. We need to formalize a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that covers performance validation across our three regions (US/EU/APAC) and a close timeline so procurement can lock in Dedicated capacity. Specifically, our stakeholders care about:

- Latency (P50/P95) for steady-state and cold-start (TTFT)
- Sustained throughput and tokens/sec under concurrency targets (50, 100, 200)
- Concurrency behavior and degradation modes (graceful degradation, queuing)
- Multi-region routing failover time and correctness (stateful KV-cache implications)

Can you share a MAP that includes an evaluation plan (test matrix, scripts/traffic profiles), and a suggested close timeline (proof-of-concept -> validation -> procurement -> go/no-go)? Attached a short request doc with our timelines.

Jordan
Jordan Ellis
Head of CloudOps, Streamline AI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask: MAP + regional perf validation

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask. I attached a first-pass MAP and a regional test matrix (see karthik_map_v1.docx and regional_test_matrix.xlsx). High-level plan below; I'll loop in Laura (performance) and Sean (reliability) for execution.

Proposed MAP + eval highlights:
- Scope: canonical LLM inferences (chat/generation) and embeddings where relevant.
- Metrics: P50/P95 token latency, end-to-end TTFT (first token cold/warm), tokens/sec throughput, success/error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV-cache hit ratios.
- Concurrency targets: 50 / 100 / 200 sustained user requests, with a 1:1 token-per-request baseline and a heavy-case 8k token sequence baseline.
- Test topology: origin client in each region hitting region-local endpoints; introduce cross-region failover by simulating AZ/region outage and observing routing + fallback model variant (smaller quantized model) behavior.
- Warmup plan: 10-minute pre-warm vs cold-start windows for TTFT measurement.
- Failover measurements: detection time, route switch latency, model cold-start when falling back, and end-to-end request error bursts.

Close timeline (suggested):
- Week 1 (POC kickoff): finalize MAP, grant test access, agree on model variants + quotas.
- Week 2 (Validation runs): run steady-state and stress profiles across us/eu/apac.
- Week 3 (Analysis & tuning): collect results, tuning (quantization, batching), and run a second validation.
- Week 4 (Commercial): finalize SOW, procurement, and go/no-go.

We can compress to 3 weeks if Streamline can allocate parallel validation teams in EU/APAC. Also, happy to include a one-time validation credit to cover cost of the tests — will confirm with finance.

Attachments: karthik_map_v1.docx, regional_test_matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <jordan@streamline.ai>
Date: 2026-06-26T15:40:00Z
Subject: MAP execution: regional perf runs + failover scenarios (action)

Team —

Jordan has asked for a MAP and validation across US/EU/APAC. Please treat this as high priority for Streamline (DEAL-4581). Two asks:

1) Laura — can you own the test execution? Key deliverables: regional latency CSV, throughput/concurrency CSV, and a short PDF summary with P50/P95 and TTFT breakdowns per region. Please run the following profiles from the regional test matrix: 8k-token heavy, 1k-token baseline, and embeddings burst.

2) Sean — reliability/failover owner. We need controlled fault injection: simulate a regional endpoint loss and measure reroute detection + end-to-end request impact. Important: capture KV-cache warmup behavior (time to reach 80% cache hit ratio after reroute).

Assumptions to validate before test:
- Model variant: rwinference-v1 (baseline) and rwinference-v1-q4 (fallback)
- Hardware: A100-equivalent for baseline; T4-equivalent for fallback; document exact instance types in results.
- Traffic shaping: steady 100r/s steady-state per region for baseline test, step to 250r/s for stress.

Please attach results and a short recommendation whether we expect to proceed with proposed Dedicated sizing for Streamline. Jordan — we'll try to have initial results within 3 business days of exec.

Karthik
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Ellis <jordan@streamline.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP execution: regional perf runs + failover scenarios (action)

Karthik / Jordan —

We completed the validation runs and attached the summary artifacts: regional_latency_report.pdf and throughput-concurrency-20260630.csv. High-level findings below. Full CSVs attached.

Summary (steady-state, rwinference-v1 on A100-equivalent):
- US (us-east): P50 token latency 47ms, P95 token latency 210ms at concurrency target 100; sustained throughput ~1,350 tokens/sec for the 1k token baseline. TTFT (warm) 42ms, TTFT (cold) 320ms.
- EU (eu-west): P50 58ms, P95 260ms; sustained throughput ~1,050 tokens/sec at conc. 100. TTFT (warm) 55ms, cold 375ms.
- APAC (asia-south): P50 72ms, P95 340ms; sustained throughput ~920 tokens/sec at conc. 100. TTFT (warm) 68ms, cold 420ms.

High-concurrency stress (250r/s step): tail amplification observed — P95 spikes up to 650ms in APAC and 480ms in EU during the 60s burst window. CPU/GPU telemetry shows transient queueing; increasing batch size/shorter batching window reduced tail by ~18% in lab re-runs.

Failover results (simulate region outage):
- Detection + routing: median 1.2s to reroute to alternative region (global routing policy); 95th percentile 2.8s.
- Model fallback: when routing to fallback model (rwinference-v1-q4 on T4-equivalent) we measured a median additional TTFT of 450ms for first request after switch (cache cold), with KV-cache reaching 80% hit ratio after ~2.6s of steady traffic.
- End-to-end user impact: short error burst (2–4% of requests) during the failover window, primarily from in-flight requests during the switch.

Recommendations:
- For Streamline's SLO (P95 < 300ms globally), plan Dedicated sizing with regional capacity headroom (target ~1.3–1.5x expected sustained tokens/sec) and conservative routing timeouts.
- Add a pre-warm step during failover (keep minimal warm pool in alternate regions) to limit TTFT penalty to <200ms.
- Consider quantized fallback model only for short tails; use it as a degraded-but-available mode rather than mainline.

Attachments: regional_latency_report.pdf, throughput-concurrency-20260630.csv

--
Laura Bennett
Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference

2) Please update the MAP to include the concrete Dedicated sizing recommendation per region (based on Laura's throughput numbers) and an explicit procurement cutoff date so we can commit this quarter.

If we get the credit and the updated MAP by EOD Friday, streamsourcing procurement will aim to sign a 12-month commit with go-live target of 2026-08-15.

Jordan
